pages.title: Mibby
pages.content:
Helping young adolescents break out of self isolation.


| Exploratory Research | Problem finding | UX Design | VL Designathon | Interaction Design | Mental Health |




A project born out of the brief shared by ValueLabs wanted us to explore how Covid 19 has changed us, study its mental and psychological effects and design for a world that is rebuilding itself.

This project (Mibby) is an attempt to first seek and then solve for the problems arising due to extensive, compulsory self isolation. This has far reaching negative impact on the social and developmental skills especially in older adolescents or teenagers that have recently arrived at college or are headed to college.

Team Janet Jacob & Shreeya Patil (My very talented colleagues from New Media Design, NID)

Role Research + Interaction design

This project was selected in the ValueLabs top 10 for the 2021 Designathon


Methods explored

  • Exploratory Research
  • Rapid Field research
  • Mental model building
  • Quick Prototyping



The pandemic has changed human behaviour. It began with the ask to isolate, then seek comfort in isolation. Now as the world opens up, we self isolate to seek comfort. 




Identifying Area of operation


To start out we brainstormed over a short session to identify the various aspects of Covid 19 related change people have observed. changes that spanned across behavior, society, group dynamics, psychological, businesses, physiology and economies.
Insight: On Identifying Anxiety and social Isolation as the two keywords that were regularly recurring, we decided to take them ahead as the direction for the solution.



We studied the different ways covid affected audiences at different levels.



Synthesis

We then built a mental model of the problem presented to simplify and understand the space we were operating within. As a part of understanding the keywords, we labeled the difference between positive self-isolation and negative self-isolation.





Self Isolation isn’t inherently a bad thing, often it is a way to disconnect and step away from our daily engagements. It is an inherent activity that we do, be it taking a run or meditating. In a positive light it is often called “Me time or solitude”.


When self Isolation is used as a coping mechanism in the face of a cognitive dissonant event, only then can it turn into a repetitive behavior and hamper emotional and personal growth in individuals.


We then identified the Target group that is the most likely to get face the adverse effects of self Isolation. Older Adolescents.



Secondary Research

A full list of the secondary research can be found below.
 Secondary research link here ︎



Primary Research

Understanding stakeholders
We also conducted a set of interviews with adults that had recently stepped away from home, during the Covid 19 pandemic, on temporary basis. This was to understand their frame of minds and what were the kind of cognitive dissonances that they ended up facing. 


Key Insights:


  1. Self Isolation at around the age of 16-19 leads to severly affected emotional development and early network building.
  2. Stepping out of home, almost every one faced problems with communication.
  3. Contrary to assumption, people felt the need to be outgoing even in the pandemic to maintain a level of relevance.
  4. We confirmed our theory of people retracting to their rooms in the face of excessive stress or anxiety.
  5. We Identified two types of people that drove these behaviors.
    1. emotionally desensitised folks
    2. emotionally hypersensitive folks



Based on these key Insights, we formulated our HMW statement.





Concept: Here are a few slides from the final solution presented at the VL Designathon 2021.
For the solution Mibby











  
The Project exploration and updates are currently viewable at quasarsmb.tumblr.com
The initial project was completed in 24 hours, with final pitch presentation made over the course of a week.

pages.title: Voice_Analytics_solution
pages.content:
Enabling better customer experiences with conversation design and voice analytics.


| Linguistics | Journey Mapping | User Research | User Experience Design | Voice analytics | Conversation design | 



In January of 2019, ︎︎︎︎︎︎︎︎* wanted to expand their set of capabilities offered to their clients. This expansion would include a service that helped do Customer experience audits, but in a holistic manner that would monitor all possible customer touchpoints.

I had the opportunity to be one of the first members within this team, working on the Voice Analytics (VA) solution.

My responsibilities included leading the research efforts in finding problems worth solving, mapping customer journey and building a frameworks for these calls, Identifying areas where digital transformation could augment the process, identifying KPIs and building a CXO level dashboard that provided actionable insights.

*Due to the nature of the contract, some of the information here has been redacted.
Client A Big–4 Consultancy (Due to an NDA, I am unable to name the company)

Role Lead Consultant, working with a team of 3, reporting directly to the solution leader. worked in tandem with a production team based out of the EU.

Timeline April 2019 - Sept 2020




Key learnings

  • Customer experience audits, Journey mapping and core UX in a business setting.
  • Breaking down linguistics workflows for indic languages.
  • Identifying KPIs that could be used to measure customer experiences
  • Working with ML engineers to build a robust system that did better transcription for indic scripts.
  • Working with data scientists to create dashboards that highlighted KPIs
  • Observing the growth of a small team to a medium size, and a service from idea to POC.
  • Preparing and giving pitch presentations to client side and customers.




The Brief was to create a SaaS based solution that automated the Quality Assurance for call centers, while monitoring all the calls.


While here, I had the opportunity to work with various technologies, and understand their place within a business. I primarily worked on the Voice Analytics segment, successfully executing a POC and adapting the solution for various sectors.


Tech under the hood

A voice analytics software primarily takes the call center audio file and analyses it to give the following outputs:

Call transcript based insights The tool transcribes the call for both channels, this in turn helps us derive events that have taken place on the calls.

Call sentiment based insights The tool identifies the tone of voice and flags the ones with the medium-high probability, which then gives an understanding of the softer aspects of the conversation.

Speech marker based insights: The tool also looks at things like rate of speech based on phonemes per second, Level of articulation, etc. along with music, speech, crosstalk and silence periods



Process

  • The Busy-eyes Report Pilot.
  • Understanding the technologies under the hood.
  • Conducting User research (Journey mapping, breaking down the call flow, building a frame work)
  • Conducting linguistic and audio analysis.
  • Synthesis and visualisation of data.
  • Designing conversational flows, and setting speech guidelines.
  • Working on the Voice Analytics Dashboard.



The Busy-eyes Report Pilot.


One of the things I worked on was the ‘Busy Eyes’ report which would be a physical version of the dashboard report.

The ‘Busy Eyes’ report was a weekly report that would provide the business an oversight into how the call center was doing. This idea was further evolved to incorporate the department-wise breakdown and the reason for calling breakdown.

The idea of these reports were modular. It would work from the ground level right up to the CXO levels.

This concept laid the foundation of the main dashboards that were eventually created as a part of the solution.



Understanding and mapping the flow of calls


Our Research consisted of the following methods

> Quantitative analysis of the calls based on the basic metadata available.
> Qualitative analysis of upto a 100+ calls to identify calling patterns. 
> Role-playing as customers to identify how special cases were handled.
> Fly-on-the wall observation of the call operators.
> Conducted Interviews with customers, operators and business  teams etc.


Synthesis

Based on the data collected, we managed to identify multiple CX painpoints.
Pain points such as: Over apology, no greetings, taking too long on call, greeting with a negative tone of voice (based on ML- sentiment analysis), etc.

With the help of this, we created an ideal flowchart of what is to be done at what level for each solution, we used this data to build over 14 KPIs and 35 Rules that drove the solution.


Helping build an Indic transcription engine

During this engagement, one of the tasks we had to do was build a dictionary of words that were to be boosted on the Transcription engine. These words included individual words, phrases to full sentences as well. 


The malleability of the spoken word


The linguistic analysis of these calls, especially the Hindi and Marathi calls lead to a robust dictionary of phrases being generated. But language is flexible, and to highlight the many ways one can speak a sentence, we had to get creative.

The linguistic inflection model was one of my key contributions while at the VA team.

Building a dashboard


We partnered with Hungarian company who would serve as our platform partners to design their platform for the needs of an Indian call center 

This was a thorough exercise over the course of 2 months that included constant to and fro with the developers to give our clients exactly what was needed. The solution created can be explored here.


The dashboard gave us a list of customers with recurring calls and negative emotions. it also looked at the customers with the most amount of escalations. There was also the scope of co-relating this information with the client-side database and arriving at high risk and low risk customers based on the spends-to-complaints proportion.



Proof of Concept

With over 14 KPIs and 35 Rules at hand, we took up a POC with one of India’s largest e-commerce. Analysing over 16,000 calls, 458 agents in English, Hindi and Hinglish.

Over the course of the 4 month long POC, we were able identify process gaps and behavior modifications that were currently leading to poor CX.


One of the main findings was that 66% calls had over empathising agents

The client had been training agents to apologise in case of any complaint being mentioned with words like 'निश्चिन्त' or ‘पूरी सहायता’. While the right response would’ve been to help the customer by solving his issue directly after acknowledging it once.









A VA solution Dashboard outling a typical call center situation



What I learned



Eventually, as the team grew my role evolved into acting as a bridge between the technology team, the business team and the clients along with slight dabbles into cloud architecture, ML.

Being the only one with a design background in the team, bringing the design-thinking structure into the team often became my role. This helped me identify my weaknesses and work on them in any consecutive project that I under took. 

As mentioned earlier, a large part of this is under an NDA. I’d be delighted to answer any questions in person if required.

pages.title: The_Centrist
pages.content:
A crowdsourced news classifier to identify bias.


| NLP | Linguistics | News | UX Design | Social Impact | New Media | GPT-3 | News Debates | 




The centrist was a project born out of an observation of the deep divide that sat within the country. The political divide out in the world was affecting situations within my extended family.

This issue was highlighted especially well in the case of the Whatsapp debates that often took place, under the guise of the 100+ notifications that would appear. Someone on one side of the family would quote a news source and talk about an event, and the reply to that would generally be someone quoting another side, and it both sides would ridicule each other’s sources.
About: Academic project done under the guidance of Mayukhini Pande and Zubin Savla

Role: Research + Digital Product Design

Timeline: April 2021 - June 2021



Key Learnings

  • Understanding Digital news consumption
  • Effects of Footfall based news on news content
  • How social media content algorithm affects polarisation
  • Shortfalls of ML based language Identification
  • How debates were conducted and the dynamics of derailing arguments



The battlefield has shifted from fake news to biased news, i.e. news that was inflammatory, clickbait and fear mongering based. Where you get your news from ensures to surround you with what you like hearing so you keep coming back.


The answer to the popular question “What radicalised you?” Is now increasingly becoming the algorithm.


Shared below is a short presentation on the problem







The Solution

How Can we fight the polarisation problem?








Arriving at the solution

Here’s a quick rundown of how this solution came to be.



Here, there, everywhere


Immersing myself in the research space I conducted thorough desk research and looked at multiple interviews, lectures and consulted books and reports.





Synthesis

3 aspects to attack
To make sense of all the wild random chaos I tried to insert a order by asking 3 fundamental questions relating to news media.




Some of the research breakdown over miro





Key findings


Why has polarisation increased

Observing the current way people were interacting with news platforms and social media, the following things became clear.
  • Print-based news papers didn’t rely on footfall or traffic
  • Relying on traffic forced news portals to write sensational-biased news.
  • Identity based polarisation has seen an increase with the rise in tailored feeds
  • Cyclic nature of the “NewsFeed” forces similar content onto readers effectively closing them in a green walled garden

How to stay unbiased?
A harder question to answer was how to stay unbiased. Originally, I looked at how debates were conducted and how they were derailed, I looked at how multiple mediums affected the conversation, I looked at what informed opinions.

  • Debates and the points they raise have a temporal nature, what seemed left-wing in 1990 is right-wing now.
  • Travel, conversation and experience ensured multiple POVs and hence well travelled people were significantly more empathetic

Solutions utilising technology.

A lot of the technology out there has been attacking the immediate evil, i.e. things like Hate speech, Fake news, misinformation, etc. The tech intervention included messaging level apps, news aggregators, and social media apps.
  • A level of internet ettiquette was needed to avoid getting hit by sensationalism, for eg. “forwarded many times” was quoted as a reason for the message to be true.
  • Banning message boards or sub-reddits would often lead to migration to other similar message boards
  • Due to the level of effort needed, fact checkers often failed. Largely becoming or being utilised by news that was quoted by other sources.
  • Labeling an article as opinion didn’t help as it was often held at the same level as factual news was.






How might we build a solution that makes a more informed citizen; who is able to identify bias and equip them with tools that help others do the same?


The How might we statement.


Exploring solutions


Before settling on the current solution I explored a couple of ideas, you can glance at the ideas below. The final exploration included a mixture of all of these.



Appendix






Conclusion

Researching this topic provided me insight into my own biases, the nature of digital news and the algorithm serving me content. I read news a little less now, and like to think I’m a little more equipped at identifying Bias.

I am on the look out for similarly minded folks that would like to help me build the centrist engine. If you think you are interested, drop me a mail!

pages.title: AmazeStudio
pages.content:
Building a No/low-Code Website builder for designers.


| Product design | UX Design | User Research | Marketing & Branding | Strategy | #Everything-Design-Related |




Amaze Studio was a sandbox product for creatives – a no-code website builder for the everyday visual designer. In the UX world our quest, often deeply rooted in pragmatism, is to create the simplest, no nonsense, most rewarding of user journeys. The consumerist nature of modern user experience design ensures that it is so. Amaze, was anything but that.

ICD was incubating a start up R Corp that was creating a design engine wich exported theHTML, JS and CSS files. It was to be called Amaze Studio. While there, I worked as the main intern on this project, conducting research to designing investor presentations to the marketing website.

Client Itu Chaudhuri Design pvt ltd.

Role Design Intern @ ICD: Diploma project under Principal designer Lisa Rath, with the help from UX Head Avi Agarwal.
In partnership with R-corp: Gaurav Ramanan

Timeline  May 2017 - Dec 2017 (Graduation Project)


Key learnings

  • First foray into working in a collaborative with a team of 10+ Devs
  • Building Information Architectures, user experience design in practice
  • Building Component sheets and Pixel perfect UI
  • Building a Pitch deck and approaching VCs
  • Product Execution from Design to Development to Testing(Rinse and Repeat)


“How might we create a tool that allows freedom to design for the web as if it were print, while allowing all the functionality that web had to offer”




Process

I arrived at ICD with the brief, the problem statement, and the first version of the product already in place.

The way forward was to
  • Conduct a usability audit
  • User study + Need assesment
  • Competition analysis
  • Identify pain points 
  • Synthesis
  • Prototypeing 
    Profit???




Exceprt from the Graduation Project Documentation

The Audit

I realised that the V1 of the software was designed to provide a front end to how code was written. While this product did all that was required from a code generator, it was clunky, hard to use, and a little overwhelming at first with the amount of tools and parameters that it required the users to take care of.

A screenshot of Amaze Studio 1.0 circa May 2017.





Diving Deeper 

While at ICD and working on the project with the startup, a lot of the research conducted was qualitative in nature. As we were stationed inside a design studio, we had an a few designers as guinea pigs to test our prototypes on, and observe them perform various tasks.

As a starting point to dive deep into the product, I conducted a Heuristic evaluation of the product based on the Nielsen method. I also conducted a fly on the wall study, observing multiple designers using the software. Conducted multiple Interviews regarding how the users went about designing

  • Vector design apps for Print (eg. Illustrator, Indesign)
  • Digital Design softwares (eg. Sketch, Figma,
  • Prototyping tools(eg Invision, Framer)
  • Website builders (eg. Squarespace, wix,)

I conducted a workflow assessment and user journey mapping of how the website would get designed, developed and deployed.

Please note that in this context, when I say design, I specifically mean the visual design of these websites.



Understanding and breaking down the programmer and the designer side of things. 


Key Insights from the audit


  • Lack of homing space
  • Lack of responsiveness - need to design multiple times
  • High cognitive load
  • Unfamiliar terminology
  • Tool usage lacked intuitiveness
  • No Shortcuts or Key bindings





To begin with we created a 3 step breakdown of the set of tasks the tool needed to perform
  1. Design : Ability to design elements in a free manner
  2. Define : Ability to define the elements that were created as web friendly entities
  3. Deploy : The ability of the tool to cleanly generate a deployable HTML5 CSS + JS code

We conducted a market study to identify and divide our competition and measure how well they were able to fulfil these prerequisites.


The Positioning exercise & competition study

After researching the user flows and conducting component breakdowns for the various competitors, I presented the findings to the studio, Image below. At this point, the Studio decided to take a Blue Ocean Strategy.

Main competition (in 2017) consisted of
• Wix, Wordpress and Squarespace
• Invision, Framer, Atomic
• Photoshop, Sketch, Illustrator
• Sketch + plugins, • Adobe Muse • Webflow

I was to design Amaze such that it would work across the verticals of Designing, Definition, and Deployment.


A brief look into the Competition study conducted.


The Amaze Clean up Plan.

While designing amaze we had to make sure that the tool we created never actually overwhelmed the user with a look and feel that would influence in anyway how the user’s creation would look. We had to take into account that the design looked appropriate no matter what the content inside the canvas was and that the Differentiation between the interface and the canvas was prominent enough that the user never felt confused between them.

After creating an IA of the existing tool, we found that many main functions were stuck inside a menu within a menu. The first course of action was to liberate these functions. While working on this, we had a secondary task to introduce functionalities like
  • Responsiveness
  • Save status
  • Preflight
  • Breadcrumbs
  • Zoom Indicator

These were essential and would help the user keep stock of where he was while editing or navigating his designs.

I spent a significant chunk of time to identify the key aspects of each component and create a cleaner Information architecture, something that didn’t suffer from the kitchen sink effect.


A Rework of the Information architecture v1 on the left and v2 on the right.

The Many visual explorations of Amaze studio 


Version Two Point Oh

One of the key highlights about the redesign was the light theme. After testing it with multiple users, a light theme put lesser cognitive overload on the user, with elements that were easier to pick up for a beginner. Hence we decided to go through with it.

Next up, I had to create an interface that promoted the content that was being designed and strike contrast in the subject and the tool. One of the main strategies to accomplish this was introducing a bottom bar, along with a top, right and left bar. This enclosed the design within a frame and ensured movement within the frame when the user navigated the space.

Lastly, we introduced a toolbox-like toolbar layout, only revealing the most needed tools on the right as we found out that using the toolbar for tools was a beginner behavior that, as the user advanced, would turn into a shortcut dominant behavior.



The final look for Amaze Studio.



Project Conclusion

By the end, since the leaders within the organisations wanted seperate directions, the team decided to sell off the Amaze architecture to one of our competitors, who could incorporate it into their products, a way for Amaze to see the sun someday. One day Amaze will rise again, but today it lays in a state of quiescence.

2021 Update: Looking back, many similar website builders have taken place where amaze couldve once stood. Could be something like Webflow, or something like editorX by wix, or Anima + Sketch, etc; It is possible that you might be using Amaze and not even know it.

pages.title: I_will_be_fine
pages.content:
I will be fine

An audio Installation






Overview

As a part of the Staging exercise at NMD, we were tasked with designing an experience. The video below is a my attempt to document what it feels like to be at the installation.

A good pair of Headphones are recommended.






Concept note:


At the bottom of every well, lies hope. The solace in the fact that, at the very bottom the only way left is up. That is what the sculpture tries to highlight.

An extremely minimal piece, “I will be fine” is an audio sculpture that relies on your ears more than your eyes. It is an experience that you slowly uncover as you move through a space, walking closer and close to this “cut”.

The 7 foot sculpture sits bare on the wall, open for the viewer to see it up close or even touch it. The space also includes a bench that allows the viewer to sit and listen to the audio loop play. Viewers may choose to listen to the whole audio experience more than once, that is if they choose to. Although, hearing it more than once is encouraged.

The sculpture was birthed by the idea the unscratchable itch, this itch we have to fix everything according to our liking. The human need for control, over our actions, and the reaction of others: and the failure to achieve it resulting in this downward spiral. This itch often manifests itself as voices in your head, voices that come from wounds. Wounds of unfulfilled expectations, desires and needs. Voices that are in your head, but the voices are not you.

At it's core, “I will be fine” is an attempt to ground the viewer. To ground them in our shared pains. It is an attempt to normalise feelings of inadequacy, something we often end up forgetting. It is a reminder to notice the voice as an other, that sits within. Lastly, it is a reminder in our human resilience, because whatever it is, you will be fine.




About

The Installation with the help of a camera blob tracks the viewer’s position in 3D space.

Triggering loops of the different sounds.










To arrive at the final product, I went through multiple experiments and 2 installations and different challenges they posed. 

Areas that were explored included Plastic surgery, zoom dysmorphia, face filters, etc.



Experiements at this stage attempted to induce dysmorphia, and a state of uncertainity.



Diving Deeper 



After looking a set of these experiments, I wanted to explore the other end of the spectrum, the more permanent aspect of this need for control.





The second concept included the idea of boids, you can see a short video of an installation that this set of readings instilled.

Boids: These software creatures that would attack you like negative thoughts. When you are on the left and are calm and peaceful when you go to the right.

Music Introduction - This was the first experiment which involved music.
Warning!: it might get loud.




Tools used: Processing + Kinect + Media Pipe + Ableton Live

 


An evolution on the previous installation. 





The Final Installation Process


The final prototype emerged from this aretefct made to explore the cut, an allegory for self harm

The final prototype included multiple versions, from a small prototype to a large 7 foot hand made one and finally a CNC machined version, you can see the various versions below.

Currently, I am focused on improving the internal design thinking workshops, with the goal of accelerating Credit Suisse's shift towards a more agile and user-centered approach.
